title: Shaan Puri on why "down" is the one trait to look for in a business or life partner
summary: Shaan argues the single most important trait in a partner is being "down": quick to commit, willing to do whatever the mission needs, and biased toward immediate action. He illustrates with his partner Ben, Greg Brockman at OpenAI, Airbnb and Uber, and explains why down partners enable pivots and high-upside bets.

principles.text: The most important trait in a partner, business or life, is being "down": flexible, mission-first, and quick to act.
principles.quote: When picking a partner, the most important thing is to find someone who is **“down”.**

principles.text: Being down is an action word, not a personality trait; down people start now and figure things out along the way.
principles.quote: Down isn’t just a personality trait (like, ‘smart’). Down is an action word. People who are down take action now. They don’t wait. They don’t overthink. They just start, and figure things out.

principles.text: Fast committers get far more shots on goal, which outweighs the occasional miss from under-thinking.
principles.quote: Even if they miss something 1 out of 10 times, they move 10x faster than over-thinkers, and so they get 10 times more shots on goal.

principles.text: A partner who flinches at uncertainty silently filters out high-upside ideas before you even raise them.
principles.quote: When your partner isn’t down, you pre-filter all the high upside paths out before they even see the light of day.

principles.text: Most great businesses pivot, and a mid-air U-turn only works if your partner is down.
principles.quote: You can only pull off that type of mid-air U-Turn if your partner is _down_. Weak stomachs can’t handle the sudden shifts.

principles.text: Great partners are not necessarily the smartest or hardest working; Ben was neither but was chosen for being down.
principles.quote: If Ben is one thing - Ben is down. No matter what comes up, he’s down for the cause, down to try it, down to start, right now.
